name: time-of-meeting
description: Find fair meeting times across time zones, with working-hour overlap, public holidays, clock changes, and date maths. Read-only, no login.

positive.description: Propose fair meeting times across three cities
positive.prompt: Find a fair time next week for a call between Copenhagen, New York, and Singapore.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns up to three slots next week, each with a score, local times for all three cities, and reasons (e.g. which city is early, late or at night). Names any public holiday that affects a slot and includes one timeofmeeting.com planner link.

positive.description: Convert one local time to two other cities
positive.prompt: What time is 3 PM in Tokyo for someone in London and São Paulo?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the matching local times in London and São Paulo for 15:00 Tokyo time today, with the date shift if the day changes, and each city's work-hour status.

positive.description: Clock changes and a holiday check
positive.prompt: When do the clocks change in the US and the EU this year, and is next Monday a holiday in Germany?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the 2026 DST start and end dates for a US city (e.g. New York) and an EU city (e.g. Berlin), and says whether next Monday's date is a German public holiday, naming it if so (regional holidays flagged as regional).

positive.prompt: How many working days are there in Denmark between December 1, 2026 and January 8, 2027? Which public holidays fall in that span?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the count of Monday-Friday days that are not Danish national holidays, strictly between the two dates by default, and lists the holidays in the span (e.g. Christmas Day, Second Day of Christmas, New Year's Day) with their local names.

positive.description: Build an invitation for a chosen slot
positive.prompt: Make a 45-minute invitation called Weekly sync for Monday 9 November 2026 at 15:00 Copenhagen time with New York and Singapore, with a Google Calendar link.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the timeofmeeting.com planner link for that slot, each city's local time and holiday status, and an add-to-Google-Calendar link for a 45-minute meeting titled Weekly sync. Nothing is created in any account.

negative.description: Writing to the user's calendar is out of scope
negative.prompt: Book this meeting directly in my Google Calendar and email the invite to my team.

negative.description: Not a time or scheduling question
negative.prompt: Write me a poem about autumn in Copenhagen.

negative.description: Too many cities for one meeting
negative.prompt: Find a meeting time for Copenhagen, London, New York, Chicago, Denver, Los Angeles, Tokyo, Sydney, and Mumbai.

review.commerce_description: Time of Meeting does not sell anything or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: 15 read-only tools for fair meeting times, work-hour overlap, time conversion, public holidays, clock changes, date maths, and planner/invitation links.

interface.longDescription:
Meeting across time zones means someone is often up early or late. Time of Meeting helps you find the overlap in working hours and pick a time that's fair to everyone.

Name two to eight cities and get up to three suggested times. Each one comes with a score and the reasons behind it. Work hours are 9:00-17:00 local. Early and late hours count against a slot, and night hours count more. A public holiday in any city lowers a slot and is named in the answer.

You can also:
- See the work-hour overlap for a single date.
- Convert a local time to other cities, or check the time now.
- List public holidays for a country, region, or city.
- See when clocks change, and whether a planned time falls in a skipped or repeated hour.
- Count days or working days, add working days to a date, find the last Friday of a month, and get ISO and US week numbers.
- Get a link that opens the meeting in the Time of Meeting planner, plus text to paste, a calendar file, an add-to-Google-Calendar link, or a QR code.

There's no login and nothing to install. Every tool is read-only and only computes answers from built-in city, time zone, and holiday data. No tool changes anything or contacts other services. Answers contain no ads.

Limitations: up to eight cities per meeting; working-day counts cover national holidays for 2026-2028; about 60 requests per minute and 2,000 per day per IP address.
